newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sacks heads of privatisation agency.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sacks heads of privatisation agency.

text.p: The government said on Friday on Friday it had sacked the board of Hungary's the state privatisation agency APV following illegal payments to a lawyer acting on its behalf.
"The governemt decided to remove the chairman of the board, the deputy chairman and all members of the board from their posts with immediate effect," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told reporters.

Kiss said the government had also initiated the removal of APV's supervisory board, a move which needs the approval of all parliamentary parties and the National Interest Coordination Council, a forum for employers and union leaders.
He said the lawyer, Maria Tocsik, received 804 million forints ($5.2 million) from APV for her role in negotiating the transfer of assets from the APV's control to local councils.
The minister in charge of privatisation, Tamas Suchman, who is also minister for industry and trade, will remain in his post.

Opposition party Young Democrats earlier this week demanded Suchman's resignation following reports that the state privatisation agency APV Rt paid 300 million forints to Tocsik for negotiating deals to transfer land to municipal authorites on its behalf.
The less the deals cost APV, the more she received, they said.

Reports submitted to Friday's cabinet meeting from APV's supervisory board at the request of Prime Minister Gyula Horn are reported to show that Tocsik received that sum during her first month of work in January but received more later.
Suchman said he did not know of the contract and while not wanting to anticipate the outcome of the inquiry, he considered the contract unethical.

Suchman, a member of the ruling Socialst party, previously minister without protfolio in charge of privatisation, took over on September 1 the helm of the Industry and Trade Ministry from Imre Dunai, who resigned quoting health reasons.
Parallel with his nomination, the government has put the supervision of the privatisation process under the Industry and Trade Ministry.
